definition: The values of a test statistic that lead to rejecting $\mathrm{H}_0$; for a binomial or Poisson test it is the tail with the largest probability under $\mathrm{H}_0$ that is still less than the significance level.
Rejecting the null hypothesis $\mathrm{H}_0$ when $\mathrm{H}_0$ is actually true: a false alarm.
Not rejecting the null hypothesis $\mathrm{H}_0$ when $\mathrm{H}_0$ is actually false; its probability can only be found for a stated true value of the parameter.
Two measurements on each subject, such as before and after, analysed by testing the differences as one sample.
The correlation $\rho$ between two variables in the whole population, estimated by the sample's $r$; testing $\mathrm{H}_0$: $\rho = 0$ assumes the data come from a bivariate normal distribution.
